entityDescription: In France, 25% of the population lives in areas subject to the flood risk. Among them, the majority lives in cities. It is a tremendous challenge for the crisis unit to operate with tools they can trust during the extreme episode and to anticipate with forecasting systems.TENEVIA brings a new vision of environmental monitoring through innovative solution that help authorities prevent flood risk. For the past 7 years, TENEVIA has been developing solutions for Measuring, Monitoring and Forecasting the evolution of rivers.When implementing flood prevention strategy based on early warning systems, the first step is to deploy sensors to observed and monitor the water in real time. Two critical features are sought : water level and flow rate.Water level sensors enable to alert the authorities of threshold exceedance. For this, TENEVIA has developed CamLevel, a sensors designed to monitor river, canal (…) by providing water level measurement and threshold detection. The idea is to make a CCTV camera become a sensor by implementing CamLevel Software within. The main benefit are :• to provide a vision of the site in order to help the crisis manager by facilitating the decision making;• To attest the quality of the measurement;• to locate the sensor further from the river and doing so, to limit the chance of being washed away.CamLevel is robust, non-immersive and operating in extreme conditions.Out of the same camera, it is possible to go further on the hydrometric information by calculating flow rate. The sensor CamFlow enable to trace thousands of surface velocity vectors out of a burst of image. By adding topographical and bathymetrical information, the sensor provides to the users velocity measurement (m/s) and flow rate (m3/s) information. This information is very useful for dimensioning protective structures (such as dikes) and calibrate models. It is however a difficult and expensive information to obtain. The second step is to anticipate the flood. Doing so, TENEVIA has developed a simulator that enable to gain time on the risings waters.The solution HydroCore, based on forecasting model simulates the behaviour of a catchment area in order to transform the precipitations into flow rate. The information provided enables cities to have valuable and accurate information on the state of the watercourse up to 48 hours before a flood.

Centrum dopravniho vyzkumu, v.v.i. (CDV), Transport Research Centre in English, is a public research institution, established according to the law 341/2005 Coll. on public research institutions, and the only one research body under the Czech Ministry of Transport. Established in 1993 as a legal successor of then federal (Czecho-Slovak) Transport Research Institute, CDV has continued in a more than 60-years tradition.
In 2007, CDV became a public research institute. Since 2014, CDV has also been an appraisal institute in the fields related to transport and civil engineering.
Present
Through its research focus, CDV – Transport Research Centre, covers the key needs of transport development in the Czech Republic at national, regional and local levels. The institute covers traditional fields, such as road safety, construction technology, maintenance, repairs and reconstruction of transport infrastructure, including geotechnical aspects and diagnostics of transport structures, impacts of transport on the environment, transport economy, multimodal transport, traffic psychology, traffic education, traffic demand modelling, management systems, geographic information systems, check-in and parking systems, telematic controlling systems, etc.
Research outcomes are directly applied in practice through different methods.

entityDescription: Future Needs Management Consulting Ltd is an interdisciplinary SME focusing on policy assessment and recommendations, on socio-economic impact and on business development for social and technical innovation solutions. Our staff has over 12 years’ experience of working in interdisciplinary teams on research and policy involving social problems. Our team leverages know-how from the fields of economics, social science, business administration and industrial design to assess social and economic impacts originating from the evolution of technologies in different fields such as information & telecommunications, education, healthcare, transport, regional development, culture and finance. We use insights gained from impact analysis studies to materialise data-driven innovation and to create sound policy. One of our core values is to pursue Responsible research and innovation (RRI) and to ensure that the projects and initiatives we are part of are aligned with this principle. RRI implies that societal actors (researchers, citizens, policy makers, business, third sector organisations, etc.) work together during the whole research and innovation process in order to better align both the process and its outcomes with the values, needs and expectations of society and includes impact metrics related to open access, gender, ethics, science education, etc. Privacy and security by design in both research, data science, and technology development is our second horizontal principle, ensuring that systems we contribute develop are as free of vulnerabilities and impervious to attack as possible and data processed always comply with the GDPR regulation. Our commercial services focus on helping our business clients develop R&D roadmaps aiming at product and service commercialisation, eliciting user requirements for the development of new products and services and supporting project management. We help our clients from the public and non-for-profit sectors to carry out Impact Assessments and policy evaluation. Future Needs also offers networking, dissemination, exploitation and community building services. We do so by working with a variety of stakeholders ranging from technical specialists, key industry players, policy-makers and citizen groups.

entityDescription: EV INBO is the contractor and legal entity of the Research Institute for Nature and Forest (INBO). INBO is an institute of the Ministry of Environment, Nature and Agriculture and is the Flemish research and knowledge centre for nature and its sustainable management and use. It has about 200 employees. Through its scientific research, INBO supports all agencies dealing with open space in the Flemish government, as well as organisations involved in nature conservation, forestry, agriculture, hunting and fishery. INBO also provides data for international reporting and publishes its results as open data. Via EV INBO, the core INBO research is supplemented, where INBO’s government-supplied financial means are insufficient for deploying a complete and future-oriented research program. This offers the possibility to tackle new research themes with immediate or mid-term policy relevance. EV INBO has been involved in several EU-projects and currently co-ordinates the ALTER-Net network.

entityDescription:
The National Institute for Research and Development in Forestry “Marin Dracea” - INCDS was established in the year 1933 under the name Forest Research and Experimentation Institute (ICEF), and during 1974-2015 period as Forest Research and Management Institute (ICAS). The Globe UAV team has been working since 2014 on the idea of using the mobile Internet for full communication with drones.
In March 2016 Globe UAV GmbH was founded as a private company without external investors.
The limitation of the range, especially in the city due to its topography and the many signal absorbing obstacles that use the usual video transmission, leads to the need to use the coverage of the mobile network.
Our focus was on the communication part without losing the human interface of the mind. The idea of an easy to use ground control station with all necessary information on one screen. Since then we have kept the 3 main parts of the flight screen: Live video takes up most of the screen, along with the map showing current position, direction, time and distance of the flight, and weather information. The third part at the bottom is the visualization of the main drone parameters: speed, power consumption, battery life.
One of our first ideas was to find a suitable drone to complete the system from one of the many drone manufacturers in Asia. Unfortunately the flight time was too short for all of them, so we decided to build drones ourselves.
The hardware design and production of each unit is now completely done in Germany.
A UAV, which should be ready for early reactions, we started to design the drones garage in 2018. We quickly gave up the idea of a beach shell-like protection for the drone and, upon request from the military, switched to a steel container, our first "SkyPort". Today we can offer drone hangars in three different sizes: mobile for integration into a truck, the standard SkyPort and the fully self-sufficient Twin Port.

The integration into alarm or dispatcher systems to optimize the pre-arm time of the operation is essential for many customers. A further option of the Globe UAV Ground Control Station is the post-processing of the video analysis in real time and the distribution of the video stream to different devices.

Customers of Globe UAVs include government agencies, security and defense companies as well as airlines and shipping companies.
Recent projects supported by Globe UAVs Transport of human tissue in the centre of Hamburg, AED transport in Greifswald, monitoring of power lines near Leipzig (all Germany).
